recipes.name: Quick Bruschetta Chicken Bake
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cubed
1 (15 ounce) can diced tomatoes with juice
1 (6 ounce) box chicken-flavored dry bread stuffing mix

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Spray a 9x13-inch glass baking dish with cooking spray.
Stir tomatoes, water, garlic, and stuffing mix in a large bowl; set aside to soften
Toss cubed chicken with salt in a large bowl; transfer onto the bottom of the baking dish. Sprinkle cheese and Italian seasoning on top of chicken. Spread the softened stuffing mixture on top.
Bake uncovered until chicken is cooked through and casserole is golden brown on top, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Bruschetta Chicken Bake
raw_recipe.description: This simple and delicious chicken and stuffing casserole with tomatoes, garlic, Italian seasoning, and mozzarella cheese tastes just like bruschetta.

video.description: If your family loves great Italian flavors, this easy and tasty hot dish will win over everyone! And your weeknight dinner prep is super simple—just mix cubed chicken with salt and spread in a baking dish. Then mix tomatoes, water, garlic and chicken-flavored stuffing mix to soften. Sprinkle mozzarella cheese and Italian seasoning on chicken, then cover with tomato stuffing mixture. Bake until chicken is done and dig in for a hearty meal!

review.reviewBody: O.K. I changed a few ingredients in this recipe....but other than that this was AMAZING!!! I doubled the cheese to 4 cups of mozzarella and used 4 fresh tomatoes from my garden rather than canned. I also used half olive oil and half water with a handful of torn basil to be more like bruschetta. I then added a TBS of balsamic vinegar reduction. (You could use plain balsamic vinegar) I used 4 garlic cloves and cut the chicken into wide strips rather than chunks. I added some dried parsley and oregano on top of the cheese and I then topped the entire dish with freshly grated parmesan cheese. This recipe turned out soooo good there was not even a crumb of it left!

After reading reviews, I tried this for myself. What a lot of other people have said is true: it tastes nothing like bruschetta, but more like an Italian-flavored chicken casserole. It's pretty good, but not as advertised. I also saw a lot of complaints about things being too salty or flavorless. To avoid your dish being overly salty, do NOT use any kind of stuffing mix that already has flavor added to it. Find the kind that's very plain, as in no seasoning at all. Most stuffing mixes already have seasoning in them, and they can be pretty salty, as they're meant to pair with a meat that has little flavor. Using plain, unseasoned stuffing will allow you to season the dish to your preference. I highly recommend using a salt, pepper, and garlic blend to season the stuffing. Adding some grated parmesan cheese doesn't hurt, either. As for the moistness of the stuffing, the trick is to have it fairly saturated with the tomato liquid/water, but not sopping wet to the point that it's mushy. If it looks a little dry to you, add a little more liquid. I actually added a little bit more water just before the dish went into the oven. The result was a top that was kind of crunchy, with the stuffing underneath being perfectly moist. A possibly relevant point on the stuffing: I used Alexa's Gluten-Free Plain Stuffing and cool water, instead of the boiling water that is usually called for. Do not just sprinkle the chicken with salt and Italian seasoning; instead, put your cut up chicken in a bowl, add a touch of oil, and use that same salt, garlic, and pepper blend, in addition to the Italian seasoning, and then toss to coat. You basically only want enough oil to help the seasoning stick. There shouldn't be any excess oil at the bottom of the bowl after you're done seasoning the chicken. I also wouldn't put the cheese on top of the chicken. Instead, mix both the chicken and the stuffing together, put it in your baking dish, bake it for about 20-25 minutes. Then pull the dish, add the cheese, and allow it to melt on top for the last 5-10 minutes of baking. When I prepared the chicken bake this way, it came out pretty good. Everyone went back for seconds and thirds.
Too much liquid. I wouldn’t add the water if I made it again or, I would make up the stove top with water and the cheese and put the tomatoes on the chicken THEN put the stove top on.

I definitely changed up the recipe to get as much flavor in as possible: 1) Marinate bite sized pieces of chicken (I used 8 thighs) in 1/2c balsamic glaze+2tbsp Worcestershire sauce+2tbsp Italian dressing+pinch salt+pinch pepper+1tbsp basil for 2hrs 2) 2 boxes stuffing+4tbsp butter+4tbsp EVOO+1/2c chicken broth+2 cans SEASONED tomatoes in juice+1tsp garlic+2tbsp basil+2tbsp balsamic 3) Layer of FRESH grated mozzarella between the two (completely cover chicken, but no more. I used a large jelly roll pan. 4) bake at 400 for 30min, remove & add a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese & a mozzarella on top. Not a whole layer. Put back in oven for 10min. 5) remove & allow everyone to put their own balsamic on when serving. Definitely not bad, would be better if the stuffing wasn't soggy underneath, BUT definitely enjoyable.

I don't like making changes... but I didn't plan for Sunday lunch!!! Sooooooo, I found this recipe! My chicken strips were frozen with no time to thaw them... I used 2 large cans of chicken from SAMs Club instead of raw chicken! I used 1 cup of water instead of chicken stock. I skipped the salt completely. I used homemade bread crumbs. I put in 2 tablespoon of chicken seasoning, I added 1 tablespoon of onion power, cause we love the added flair in everything!!! I had 1 cup of mozzarella cheese, 1 cup of Monterey Cheese, and 1/4 cup of Parmesan cheese so I put those all in!!! Next problem... still short on time I threw it all into a pressure cooker and cooked for 15 mins, stirred and cooked 10 more minutes!!! Delishious!!! Not watery!!! I will add one more can of tomatoes next time(I only use the seasoned chopped tomatoes!!!)

I have made this a couple of times now, and it was good, but it turned out very watery/soupy for me when I followed the directions. So after the first time of following the directions, I changed it up a bit to suit my family. I mix 4 cut up chicken breasts with a can of diced tomatoes (with garlic and olive oil), along with the additional minced garlic and some salt and pepper. I then put that mixture into my 3 qt casserole dish and baked it in the oven for 20 minutes. While that mixture was baking I prepared the stuffing on its own separately. After the 20 minutes of baking, I spooned out the excess liquid from the dish. I then sprinkled on a little dried basil, followed by a layer of mozzarella cheese, and then topped with the prepared stuffing mixture. I then put the casserole dish back in the oven for an additional 10 minutes. My family of 4 much preferred it this way, as the casserole was not watery, but still moist.

I made this according to the directions. It had good flavor but the stuffing was a little too dry. Instead of cooking for 30 minutes I put a digital remote thermometer into the thickest piece of chicken and it only took about 16 minutes for the chicken to be done and the cheese melted. It wasn't too salty but i used diced tomatoes with no salt added. I will make this again but I want to find a way to moisten the stuffing. Other than that, good dish – thank you.

I made this, but changed it up a bit due to a lot of comments on it being too dry. First, I roasted a whole chicken with butter and minced garlic. Then I used the drippings in with the chicken on the first layer, so the chicken would be moist and succulent. I then layered the chicken with mozerella. I then cooked the stuffing on the stove top and added the diced tomatoes to it. I noticed it was a bit too watered down, so I added about half a cup of garlic bread crumbs to the stuffing (until I got that perfect soft, yet crumbly texture). Then I put that on top of my mozerella, and topped it with the remainder of cheese. Since everything was precooked I cooked my case role for only 20 min (until cheese was melted). The way I made it turned out so tasty! Thank you for the recipe and I look forward to adding this as a family favorite. :)

7/3/20 Better even though I forgot the hot pepper flakes. Doubled recipe using 1 cup chicken broth and 1/4 balsamic vinegar with the rest as noted in my 2017 review. Still a bit dry so will probably up the chicken broth next time.
11/06/2017 Very good. Did double the recipe and replaced 1/4 cup of the water with balsamic vinegar. Tossed the chicken in Italian seasoning and garlic powder. Added hot pepper flakes to the tomatoes. Did not add salt. Easy. Would make again but does need more moisture.

We used 3 large chicken breasts, We drizzled the chicken with Italian dressing. We also added the garlic and Italian Seasoning to the chicken. You definitely have to double the amount of cheese in the middle and add more to the top (shredded parm is super). We baked ours for 45 minutes...30 minutes covered with foil then uncovered the pan and sprinkled with more cheese and back into the oven for 15 minutes. We loved it!

I thought this was really good. However I did omit the salt on the chicken and put onion and garlic powder, crushed red and black pepper on the chicken. I added some fresh tomatoes with a can of Italian tomatoes and next time I make this I would only use fresh tomatoes no canned at all. Also added parmesan to the top the last ten minutes of cooking and added chopped red onion to the tomato mixture. Will make again.

This was delicious! Followed the recipe pretty closely. Only changes I made were splitting the cheese, putting half on top of the chicken and adding the other half for the last 10 minutes on top of the whole dish. Hubby and I both loved it! Will definitely be adding this to our list! Thank you!
This is an amazing recipe. I have made this over and over so delicious. I use Pepperidge farm stuffing in the bag and a can of petite diced tomatoes. I keep it for sure.
Really good. Made almost as directed except I used fresh tomatoes and Italian croutons crushed because that's what I had on hand. Also drizzled with evoo before baking.
